Theme

communion noun

Holy Communion

also Holy Communion, the Eucharist, take communion, receive communion, the Lord’s Supper

late Latin

Aug. Ep. 54.6 (Lewis & Short: sānctī altāris)

commūniō, commūniōnis f.

noun, third declension

Holy Communion

Classically a sharing (Cic.); in the Church, communion and then the sacrament itself (Lewis & Short). To receive communion is commūnicāre (Aug.; Lewis & Short) or Eucharistiam sūmere (Levi–Bini). In the Byzantine rite communion is given with leavened bread and the wine together, from a spoon; in the Latin rite with unleavened bread, the host, often under one kind.

Other words

  • Eucharistia, Eucharistiae f. — the Eucharist

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Cypr. Ep. 10 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. service: mass: eucharist; Levi–Bini p. 17, s.v. comunione

    Greek εὐχαριστία, thanksgiving: the sacrament, and the Lord’s Supper itself (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Calix benedictiōnis, cui benedīcimus, nōnne commūnicātiō sanguinis Chrīstī est? et pānis quem frangimus, nōnne participātiō corporis Dominī est?

    The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? And the bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of the Lord?Vulg. 1 Cor. 10.16

See also Mass, the Divine Liturgy, confession, church.
